# conveyor_service_account_token (Resource)

A credential token for a service account. This resource tracks only non-secret metadata: use the `conveyor_service_account_token` ephemeral resource to read the token's secret, which is never persisted to state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: fully automatic token rotation, writing the current token secret into an AWS SSM
# parameter without the secret ever touching Terraform state.
#
# Steady state has exactly one live token. A new one is minted every `rotation_days`; the previous
# one is retired `grace_period_days` after its own mint, giving consumers time to pick up the new
# value before the old one is revoked. Keep grace_period_days < rotation_days so a mint tick and a
# retire tick never land in the same apply under normal cadence. Apply at least once per grace window,
# or a sparse apply can land both in the same run (resulting in a brief, single-apply-duration gap).

terraform {
  required_providers {
    time = {
      source = "hashicorp/time"
    }
    aws = {
      source = "hashicorp/aws"
    }
  }
}

variable "rotation_days" {
  default = 30
}

variable "grace_period_days" {
  default = 3
}

resource "conveyor_service_account" "my_service_account" {
  name            = "my_service_account"
  type            = "scoped"
  project_ids     = [conveyor_project.my_project.id]
  environment_ids = [conveyor_environment.my_environment.id]
}

resource "time_rotating" "mint" {
  rotation_days = var.rotation_days
}

locals {
  current_generation = time_rotating.mint.unix

  # This reconstructs the previous generation from the current mint time, which assumes you apply
  # at least once per rotation period. If you might skip an apply across an entire rotation
  # boundary, persist mint history explicitly instead (for example with a `terraform_data`
  # resource) rather than recomputing it here.
  previous_mint_time  = timeadd(time_rotating.mint.rfc3339, "-${var.rotation_days * 24}h")
  previous_deadline   = timeadd(local.previous_mint_time, "${var.grace_period_days * 24}h")
  previous_generation = timecmp(timestamp(), local.previous_deadline) < 0 ? tostring(local.previous_mint_time) : null

  generations = compact([tostring(local.current_generation), local.previous_generation])
}

resource "conveyor_service_account_token" "rotating" {
  for_each = toset(local.generations)

  service_account_id = conveyor_service_account.my_service_account.id
}

# Always sourced from the most-recently-minted, not-yet-retired generation.
ephemeral "conveyor_service_account_token" "current" {
  service_account_id = conveyor_service_account.my_service_account.id
  client_id          = conveyor_service_account_token.rotating[tostring(local.current_generation)].client_id
}

resource "aws_ssm_parameter" "service_account_token" {
  name = "/my-app/service-account-token"
  type = "SecureString"

  value_wo         = ephemeral.conveyor_service_account_token.current.secret
  value_wo_version = local.current_generation
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `service_account_id` (String) The id of the service account this token belongs to.

### Read-Only

- `client_id` (String) The client id of the token, generated on creation.
- `created_at` (String) The RFC3339 timestamp at which the token was created.
- `id` (String) The id of this resource, in the form `service_account_id/client_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
export SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID=$(conveyor service-account get --name my_service_account -ojson | jq -r ".id")
export CLIENT_ID=$(conveyor service-account token list --service-account-id "$SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID" -ojson | jq -r ".[0].client_id")
terraform import 'conveyor_service_account_token.rotating["<generation-key>"]' "$SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID/$CLIENT_ID"
```
